name: Nimzo-Indian Defense
description: A positional defense that teaches pinning, central pressure, and structural imbalances.

branches.title: Main Line: Pin With Bb4

moves.title: White starts d4
moves.explanation: White controls central squares. d4 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. The Nimzo uses the pin to pressure e4 and sometimes trades bishop for knight to damage structure.

moves.title: Develop knight
moves.explanation: Black controls e4 and d5. Nf6 develops a knight to f6. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.title: White expands
moves.explanation: White builds queen-pawn space. c4 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. The Nimzo uses the pin to pressure e4 and sometimes trades bishop for knight to damage structure.

moves.title: Prepare Bb4
moves.explanation: Black opens the bishop and supports central dark squares. e6 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. The Nimzo uses the pin to pressure e4 and sometimes trades bishop for knight to damage structure.

moves.title: White supports center
moves.explanation: White develops the knight in front of the c-pawn. Nc3 develops a knight to c3. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.title: Pin the knight
moves.explanation: Bb4 pins the c3 knight and fights for e4. This is the Nimzo-Indian idea. Bb4 develops a bishop to b4. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.title: Shape the center
moves.explanation: e3 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. The Nimzo uses the pin to pressure e4 and sometimes trades bishop for knight to damage structure.

moves.title: Get the king safe
moves.explanation: O-O moves the king to safety and brings the rook closer to the center. This is usually the moment when the opening becomes an early middlegame plan: The Nimzo uses the pin to pressure e4 and sometimes trades bishop for knight to damage structure.

moves.title: Develop to f3
moves.explanation: Nf3 develops a knight to f3. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.title: Shape the center
moves.explanation: d5 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. The Nimzo uses the pin to pressure e4 and sometimes trades bishop for knight to damage structure.

moves.title: Improve with a3
moves.explanation: a3 is a quiet improving move. Quiet moves matter when they finish development, prevent counterplay, or prepare a clear next plan.

moves.title: Shape the center
moves.explanation: c5 clarifies the pawn structure. Central moves should claim space, challenge a pawn, or prepare a break. The Nimzo uses the pin to pressure e4 and sometimes trades bishop for knight to damage structure.

hints: Follow the highlighted move and say the idea out loud.
After each move, check king safety, center control, and piece activity.
When a trade appears, ask what file opens and which piece improves next.
coachingNotes: Learn the default Nimzo-Indian setup.
The Nimzo uses the pin to pressure e4 and sometimes trades bishop for knight to damage structure.
Good trades usually remove an active enemy piece, open a useful file, or simplify once your king is safe.
After the opening, do not drift: improve your worst piece, connect rooks, and look for one clear pawn break.

moves.title: White questions bishop
moves.explanation: White attacks the bishop. a3 is a practical improving move for White. In real games, keep asking: is my king safe, are my pieces active, and what central pawn break comes next?

moves.title: Recommended: capture
moves.explanation: Bxc3+ gives up the bishop pair but damages White's structure and keeps long-term pressure. Bxc3+ shows how trades enter the opening. This is an equal trade. Equal trades are good when they improve your structure, open a file, or remove an active enemy piece. After a trade, ask which file opened and which piece should improve next.

moves.title: Trade or capture on c3
moves.explanation: bxc3 shows how trades enter the opening. This wins material, so the trade is clearly favorable if the piece cannot be trapped afterward. After a trade, ask which file opened and which piece should improve next.

moves.explanation: Qc2 is a supportive queen move after development has started. The queen helps connect rooks and protect key squares instead of wandering out early.

commonMistakes: Capturing on c3 without understanding why.
Stopping after memorized moves and playing without a plan.
Trading automatically without asking what improves afterward.
Starting an attack before castling or finishing development.
